prompt: For the parabola $y = x^2$, what is $y$ when $x = -4$?
hint: Squaring means multiplying a number by itself. Think about the sign you get when the number is negative.

hints.text: Squaring means multiplying a number by itself. Think about the sign you get when the number is negative.
Put in $x = -4$ to get $y = (-4) \times (-4)$. A negative times a negative gives a positive.
$(-4) \times (-4) = 16$, so the value of $y$ is $16$ when $x$ is $-4$.

explanation: Substitute $-4$ for $x$, keeping it in parentheses: $y = (-4)^2 = (-4) \times (-4)$.
A negative number times a negative number is positive, so the product is $16$.
So $y = 16$, the same height as at $x = 4$. That is why the parabola is symmetric.

alternativeExplanations.title: Mirror twins on the U
steps: On the parabola, x = 4 and x = −4 sit at the same height, like mirror twins.
Since 4² = 16, the twin −4 also lands at y = 16.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table of values
steps: The left side copies the right side — read off y = 16 at x = −4.
